project_context: Local LLM Memory is a fully local, privacy-preserving AI coding assistant that combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with natural-language file and function operations via Ollama, ChromaDB, and structured intent routing.

architecture.title: high_level
architecture.description: Interactive Python REPL / CLI ➔ Structured LLM Intent Parser ➔ Route Dispatcher (Filesystem Ops) OR RAG Retriever (ChromaDB) ➔ Ollama Local LLM (Mistral)

architecture.title: infrastructure
architecture.description: 100% On-Premise / Local Host Execution via Ollama (localhost:11434) with local PyTorch sentence-transformer embeddings.

architecture.title: design_paradigm
architecture.description: Dual-path architecture separating natural language filesystem mutations from vector-searched conversational code context.

architecture.title: asset_delivery
architecture.description: Local file system operations scoped securely within defined project roots with strict traversal protection.

problem.title: Problem
problem.description: Standard LLM chat models suggest code changes but cannot execute file operations, while generic commands often fail due to unstructured natural language.

solution.title: Solution
solution.description: Architected a dual-stage intent parser that extracts structured JSON payloads from raw prompt text and dispatches commands directly to local handlers.

technical_details.title: Technical Details
items: Leveraged Mistral via Ollama to classify queries into code/doc RAG requests or actionable file/function mutations.
Implemented an SHA-1 query caching system (`intent_cache.json`) to skip LLM classification calls for identical prompts.
Added multi-intent extraction and priority sorting to execute prerequisite file creation steps before subsequent reads or modifications.

outcome.title: Impact
items: Eliminated the need to manually copy-paste code suggestions by executing code operations directly from plain English.
Reduced LLM processing overhead through deterministic intent caching.

problem.title: Problem
problem.description: Large codebases exceed model context limits, while mixing source code and documentation in a single vector collection dilutes search precision.

solution.title: Solution
solution.description: Constructed an intent-aware dual vector retrieval engine that segregates source code and markdown documentation into dedicated ChromaDB collections.

technical_details.title: Technical Details
items: Engineered file chunking using `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter` (500 chunk size / 100 overlap) tuned for source code syntax.
Embedded code and documentation using local HuggingFace BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings.
Implemented automated checks (`index_utils.py`) that trigger offline sub-process index builds if database collections are missing.

outcome.title: Impact
items: Delivered relevant codebase context to local models within limited context windows.
Maintained 100% data privacy by running all embeddings and vector lookups on local hardware.

problem.title: Problem
problem.description: User prompts frequently contain typos or partial directory paths, causing traditional direct path filesystem lookups to crash or execute outside the project.

solution.title: Solution
solution.description: Developed a fuzzy path resolution engine paired with a sandboxed file dispatcher that translates approximate names into safe, relative project paths.

technical_details.title: Technical Details
items: Maintained an offline `structure_index.json` map of all folders and files relative to the codebase root.
Integrated `difflib.get_close_matches` to resolve approximate directory inputs (e.g., matching 'sever' to 'server/').
Enforced strict path normalization (`resolve_codebase_path`) in `config.py` to prevent directory traversal attacks (e.g., `../`).

outcome.title: Impact
items: Prevented filesystem access errors caused by user typos during conversational code creation.
Guaranteed complete file safety by locking all system operations within the target project directory.
